speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have an initial report marked as untrusted, but I will rely on your direct description today. To begin, can you describe the skin lesion(s) you are concerned about, including their location, size, shape, and any changes in color or texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Penis (and likely Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the finger).

The combination of a non-healing, crusty lesion on the penile shaft in a 62-year-old male with a significant smoking history and a similar lesion on his finger is highly suspicious for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, particularly given the lack of response to prior treatments. Given the location and potential for malignancy, I need to confirm the diagnosis immediately. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_penile_lesion; Biopsy_of_finger_lesion.
